questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. When resorption stops in a resorption canal, a cement line is deposited at the periphery. The formation of a new Haversian system (osteon) begins with the first lamella deposited on the cement line, and growth of the ostein proceeds centripetally.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue shown in this image.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Two criteria are used for classifying bone tissue: (1) the amount of bony tissue versus non-bone tissue (spongy vs compact); and (2) if the matrix has lamellae (woven vs lamellar). In this image, non-bone tissue (bone marrow) predominates, the matrix is amorphous and the osteocytes appear randomly arranged.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the clear-staining layer indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Osteoid, the organic matrix, is deposited first during bone formation and appears as a narrow, pale strip on the bone surface beneath active osteoblasts. The inorganic matrix is deposited in the osteoid.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Lacunae are small spaces in bone where osteocyte cell bodies are/were located.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the epiphyseal zone enclosed by the outline.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. During endochondral ossification, hyaline cartilage becomes calcified and nutrients cannot reach the chondrocytes. Consequently, the chondrocytes degenerate and die, leaving behind the calcified cartilage spicules surrounding the chondrocyte lacunae. These remaining spicules form a framework on which bone can be deposited.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the epiphyseal zone that fills the outline.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. In the zone of ossification, woven bone is deposited on the surface of the calcified cartilage spicules. The red-staining bone can be easily differentiated from the purple, calcified cartilage spicules. No osteoclasts are present, so this is not be the zone of resorption.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Volkmann's canals run perpendicular to and interconnect the Haversian canals, transporting blood vessels between the adjacent Haversian systems.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures identified by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The osteon, or Haversian system, consists of concentric layers of bone deposited centripetally around a central Haversian canal.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells at the tips of the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Osteocytes are osteoblasts that have completely surrounded themselves with bony matrix. In this woven bone they show a random arrangement and more rounded lacunae than they would in mature, lamellar bone.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells at the tips of the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Active osteoblasts are cuboidal in shape and lie directly on developing bone. They are actively secreting osteoid, the organic component of bone.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layers indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The external surface of the diaphysis of a long bone is frequently lined by outer circumferential lamellae, which increase the thickness of the diaphysis. The convex curvature of this surface indicates that these lamellae are the outer, rather than the inner, circumferential lamellae. These lamellae were deposited by intramembranous bone formation by the osteogenic layer of the periosteum.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This compact bone is composed of both woven and lamellar bone. This area shows circumferential lamellae at either side as well as a central area of the former zone of ossification, where osteons have filled the spaces between the calcified cartilage-woven bone spicules in the zone of ossification.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. New bone is deposited on internal bony surfaces by an endosteum possessing active osteoblasts. This forming osteon is lined by such an endosteum and is depositing new bony lamellae on pre-existing bone.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows
In life what would occupy the hair-like structures at the tips of the arrows?

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. At high magnification of a ground bone preparation, the lacunae (housing osteocytes) and canaliculi (housing osteocyte processes radiating from the osteocytes) are very distinct.

questoes.enunciado: What is the function of the cell at the tips of the arrows?

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Osteoclasts, large cells with multiple nuclei and pink-staining cytoplasm, breakdown (resorb) bone. Osteoclasts, not related to osteoblasts or osteocytes, lie in the endosteum on external and internal bony surfaces.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Resorption canals have irregular outlines, contain a blood vessel, and are lined with an endosteum containing osteoclasts. They have no concentric lamellae. These canals form the eroding tips of columnar-shaped remodeling units, which are oriented parallel to the long axis of the bone.

questoes.enunciado: What type of bone formation produced the bone at the tips of the arrows?

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The periosteal collar indicated by the arrows is formed by intramembranous bone formation because this bone was deposited on, rather than replacing, the original cartilage template. The template undergoes endochondral bone formation as evidenced by the epiphyseal plates at either end of the marrow space. The periosteal collar supports the forming bone and contributes to its future diaphysis.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The osteogenic layer of the periosteum lies internal to the fibrous layer and adjacent to the bone. The osteogenic layer contains osteoblasts that deposit bone, osteoclasts that resorb bone and flattened endosteal cells. All cell types are present in these images

questoes.enunciado: What type of growth occurs at this site?

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT! This image shows the periosteum which deposits bone by intramembranous ossification on the surface of existing bone, which is an example of appositional growth.
